findings.reason: the cursor is the whole mechanism by which delivery is exactly once per pane; leaving its identity undefined across partitions sends the node to a design that either replays rows after a rollover or silently drops them after retention.
findings.text: §8 has the subscriber "select the rows for its session and the broadcast rows after its cursor", but §5 (line 133) writes events into one file per UTC day and their `id` is per-partition, while §5's retention unlinks a partition older than seven days; nothing defines what a cursor value identifies across partitions, nor what a subscriber does when the partition holding its cursor has been unlinked, so the re-armed-subscriber clause at line 213 ("continues from its cursor with no `new →` row" for a pane already drawn) has no defined source of truth, and the subscriber must also `ATTACH` the partitions spanning its cursor and re-attach at the UTC rollover — a read path §8 never names

findings.reason: as written the node's own gate is unpassable, and the plan must either move the subscriber's registration into §5's node-local root or exempt it explicitly from the measure.
findings.text: §8 asserts the follower "computes no snapshot, reads nothing on GPFS", while the same section's done-when requires the freshness case to assert the subscriber's "registration in place" (line 212); the follower's registration is the watch record `crew_home()/watch/<project>-<digest>.lock` read by `_read_watch_record` (reckon/crew/run_paths.py:24, reckon/crew/follower_registration.py:299) and the crew home is the GPFS-backed config home, so the 60 s no-crew-home-reads measure at line 216 and the registration requirement cannot both hold

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `tests/test_a_delivered_row_does_not_round_trip.py`, `tests/test_a_dispatch_is_one_row.py`, `tests/test_crew_session_delivery.py`, `tests/test_follower_freshness.py` (its `test_running_follower_reloads_without_stream_or_registration_gap` at line 172) and `ticker.PaneRowPath` (reckon/crew/ticker.py:1907) all resolve; `reckon/crew/station_store.py` is declared new by §5, so its absence is expected.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §8's done-when is measurable in every clause (named existing tests, a retargeted reload case, four enumerated new tests, a 60 s `/proc/<pid>/io` delta) and it declares a negative control ("a subscriber that does not persist its cursor must fail the restart test").
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §8's gate is the repository's test suite plus a per-process `/proc/<pid>/io` delta recorded in the run's own gate log; no clause sends evidence to a session scratchpad or a node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §8 introduces no symbol, filename, comment or docstring carrying a plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag; §1's `old §77`/`old §86` are plan-internal cross-references in prose, not code.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §8's subscriber cannot resolve "the rows … after its cursor" against §5's per-day event partitions, and §8's "reads nothing on GPFS" is contradicted by its own requirement that the subscriber's registration be in place, where that registration is a crew-home watch record.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §8 carries one deliverable, `crew follow` becomes a subscriber; the pane-policy move into the station is the stated precondition for the row it renders and not a second outcome.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-depends-on` is acyclical and each edge matches the narrative: s8 depends on s7 (the subscriber reads the station §7 creates), s9/s10 depend on s7, and s12 depends on s8–s11; the open followup `f-tmref-002` ("§6 waits on §5 … and §7 follows §6") now agrees with the graph.
